season.source: https://www.summerscountywv.gov/parksandrec ('Within the boundaries of the Bluestone Wildlife Management area sits several primitive campgrounds: Bertha, Cedar Branch, Shanklin Ferry, and Mouth of Indian Creek ... Each of the camping areas are open seasonally May through November, water levels permitting'), read 2026-10-21

note: Summers County-run primitive camping area strung along the south bank of the New River at the end of Cedar Branch Road, across from Crumps Bottom, inside Bluestone Wildlife Management Area. Fire rings and some tables. CAVEATS: nobody has reported what size rig fits - sites are dirt pads reached by gravel county roads, so scout before bringing EKKO in; the area floods in high water and parts may flood more often during the ongoing Bluestone Dam work (DNR District 4, 304-256-6947, has gate-closure updates). --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: kept, though we can't tell whether the sites suit RVs. --Claude
summary: County Parks & Rec page confirms Cedar Branch as one of its four primitive Bluestone WMA campgrounds at $15/night/site (fees already manual) and gives the season: changed season year_round:false -> May-November (water levels permitting). DNR's WMA map labels 'Cedar Branch Campground'; WVU's DIY Outdoors says the Summers County Commission runs the camping areas, so ownership local stands. Not stated on any operator page: site count, rig size, toilets, reservations (derived values left). Note trimmed of the hookups/water/reservation/fee/season restatements.
flags: Conflicting DNR page: WV DNR's District 4 WMA page (https://wvdnr.gov/lands-waters/wildlife-management-areas/district-4-wildlife-management-areas/, read 2026-10-21) says under '51. Bluestone Lake' 'On the WMA: Camping is not permitted', while DNR's own Bluestone WMA map labels 'Cedar Branch Campground' and Summers County lists it with a $15 fee. Probably stale boilerplate on the DNR page, but a human may want to confirm.
Criteria (already accepted by AWH 2026-10-11): no operator or agency page says whether a 23-ft motorhome fits; the county page says only 'primitive camping only'.
